items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (George Handy) does not mention Jack McKenney in any of his turns. McKenney is only mentioned by the Interviewer and a Voice as someone who made comments about Handy or the music scene.

ctx.x: The planned recording session was the one of all the new music. It would have been "Dalvatore," "There's No You", "Out of This World," "Gray Suede," "Hey Look I'm Dancing," "Key F" and two more; "Memphis In June" and "Over The Rainbow." When I got back the only ones they had done were "Dalvatore" and half of "Over The Rainbow"; the other half was completed by--I find it hard to believe that it was Max Steiner. Why Max Steiner would have wanted to involve himself with the second half of a jazz band chart I could…
Nobody else--I guess Jack McKenney--said that he thought it was Johnny
Richards, but Johnny Richards wasn't on the scene then, was he?
